definitions.gloss: candied dried baby sardines; another name for {田作|たづく}り
definitions.explanation: Small dried sardines roasted and coated in a sweet soy glaze, eaten at New Year. The same dish as {田作|たづく}り; ごまめ is the name used in western Japan and in older cookbooks.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎年|まいとし}ごまめを{作|つく}っていた。
examples.english: My grandmother used to make gomame every year.

examples.japanese: {関東|かんとう}では{田作|たづく}りと{呼|よ}ぶが、{関西|かんさい}ではごまめと{言|い}うことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In the Kanto region it is called tazukuri, but in Kansai it is usually called gomame.

notes:
Sometimes written {五万米|ごまめ} with characters chosen for their auspicious meaning rather than their sound value.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Dried sardines were once spread on rice paddies as fertilizer, which is why the dish is also called {田作|たづく}り ("field-making"). Either way the dish is a wish for a good harvest, and it is one of the three celebratory dishes of {関東|かんとう}-style おせち{料理|りょうり}.

RELATED EXPRESSION:
- ごまめの{歯|は}ぎしり: "a small fry grinding its teeth" — a weak person fuming uselessly at something beyond their power
